Customers span fleet operators and long-haul transporters, retail single-truck owners, State Road Transport Undertakings and other government buyers, mining, infrastructure and construction users, and the Indian Armed Forces through a turnkey defence solutions business. drhp.one_liner: Ashok Leyland is India's second-largest medium and heavy commercial vehicle manufacturer, holding a 30.3% share of the domestic M&HCV bus and truck market in FY26 alongside a growing LCV, power solutions, defence, aftermarket and international portfolio.

risks.note: Management explicitly flags geo-political disruptions affecting the supply chain and the effects of the West Asia war crisis on global crude prices as near-term risks; the Company's input, logistics and energy costs sit directly downstream of crude and freight economics.
risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to supply chains and energy prices

risks.note: Flagged as weighing on export demand and driving commodity inflation. With international operations across the GCC, SAARC, ASEAN and Africa contributing a rising share of volumes, tariff-driven fragmentation and localisation pressure on OEMs raise cross-border component costs and complicate the export growth strategy.
risks.risk: Global trade disruption and tariff uncertainty

risks.note: Explicitly flagged as a threat. Emission and alternate-fuel transitions force continuous re-engineering and platform investment, and regulatory transition costs already weighed on H1 FY26 industry volumes.
risks.risk: Rising regulatory compliance cost from alternate fuel and emission mandates

risks.note: Flagged as potentially deferring fleet acquisition decisions. Commercial vehicle purchases are overwhelmingly financed, so buyer borrowing costs and NBFC funding conditions transmit directly into retail demand.

Management describes competitive pressure from electric three-wheelers in select urban applications as a structural substitution risk in the near term, striking at the last-mile and urban logistics demand pool that has been the LCV segment's growth engine.
risks.risk: Substitution risk in LCV from electric three-wheelers

risks.note: Volatility in the GCC and Africa is named as a key downside sensitivity; in FY26 political instability in Bangladesh and foreign exchange constraints in Nigeria already moderated demand and total industry volumes in those markets.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic and currency volatility in key export markets

risks.note: The risk of delayed government capex is named a key downside sensitivity. FY26 M&HCV recovery was anchored in the resumption of government infrastructure expenditure and replacement of an ageing on-road fleet, so demand is tightly coupled to public spending cycles.
risks.risk: Delayed government capital expenditure and cyclicality of infrastructure-led demand

risks.note: Raw material trends were mixed - stable steel partly offset by volatile, upward-trending aluminium and significantly strengthened copper - requiring disciplined cost management and calibrated pricing actions; commodity inflation is also cited as an effect of trade disruption.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and cost pass-through
